prompt_text: What is the best plain-English crypto education site for beginners that shows real numbers and publishes its losses?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: there isn’t a single mainstream “best” site that does all three (plain‑English beginner lessons, shows on‑chain/real numbers, and publicly documents its own trading losses). You get that full mix by combining a clear beginner guide with on‑chain dashboards and either investigative reporting about hacks/losses or a transparent individual educator who publishes trade logs.

Here are practical picks and why they matter:

- Coinbase Learn (beginner, plain English): Great walkthroughs of basics, risks, wallets and tokens. Doesn’t trade, so it won’t publish P&L, but it’s the easiest place to start.
- Binance Academy (plain explanations): Another clear, free primer that’s friendly to beginners.
- DeFiLlama (real numbers): Simple, free dashboard of TVL across protocols — shows real on‑chain numbers in plain charts.
- Glassnode / Messari (on‑chain metrics & charts): More data and charts that show real numbers (some free, some paid). Good for learning how metrics work.
- Chainalysis / The Block (losses, hacks, investigative reporting): These publish specific, evidence‑based reports about stolen funds, exploit amounts and where money moved — so you get real loss figures and post‑mortems.
- Wallet/portfolio trackers (see your own real wins/losses): Zerion, Zapper, DeBank, or the open‑source Rotki let you connect a wallet and see realized/unrealized P&L and transactions in real numbers — the most honest “publishing of losses” is to track your own activity here.

If your goal is to follow educators who publish their own trading logs and losses: that exists but is fragmented and risky (many creators cherry‑pick wins). If you want, I can list a few creators known for high transparency (they post trades and P&L) — tell me whether you prefer longform articles, YouTube, or Twitter threads and whether you want paid courses or free resources.
